title: POC Weekly Sync - throughput optim
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput tuning results. We increased concurrency and adjusted continuous batching; saw a 30% throughput uplift at cost of 10% higher p95 tail latency for longer sequences. Agreed next benchmark with 10k requests and to test queueing policy changes on dedicated/NATed VPC cluster. Action items: run larger load test, share runbook and updated metrics dashboard, follow up on pricing implications for dedicated cluster.
topics: next benchmarks and dedicated cluster testing
next_steps: Redwood to run 10k-request throughput benchmark (include 2x long sequences)
Customer to enable dedicated test VPC on Friday and share access details
Redwood to send updated cost delta spreadsheet for concurrency increase
Schedule deep dive with infra team next Tuesday if results unstable
action_items: Maya Chen: share benchmark config and runbook (due 2026-12-24)
Arjun Patel: run 10k-request throughput test and upload results to shared sheet (due 2026-12-24)
Sara Gomez: provision dedicated test VPC and confirm network egress rules (due 2026-12-25)

transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, this is our weekly POC throughput sync, we have Arjun and Noah on from Redwood.
[00:18] Joanna Park: Hi all, Joanna here, quick note, we've got Sara and Liam as well. We just want to understand the tradeoffs for higher concurrency.
[00:28] Maya Chen: Great. Quick agenda: recap last week's changes, numbers from the test run, tuning we did for continuous batching, and then queueing policy.
[00:40] Arjun Patel: Alright, recap — last week we bumped concurrency from 8 to 16 for the inference pool, enabled continuous batching with a target batch window of 12ms and set max_batch to 48. We also turned on prefix KV cache for repeated prefixes.
[00:58] Liam O'Neal: Quick clarification — prefix KV cache, is that the same as the kv cache in the docs or you changed something?
[01:05] Arjun Patel: Yeah it's the same concept, but we tuned eviction and warmup heuristics; there might be some mis labelling in the logs, sometimes it shows as "kvash" in the agent logs, ignore that.
[01:18] Joanna Park: Okay, what were the numbers after the change?
[01:22] Arjun Patel: So baseline last week — about 1.2k tokens/sec sustained at p50 with concurrency 8. After changes, peak throughput went to ~1.6k tokens/sec, roughly a 30% uplift. Cost per token rose by ~9% in the short run because more GPU units were active more often.
[01:42] Sara Gomez: What happened to latency p95? We saw some tail spikes during long sequences yesterday in our smoke run.
[01:49] Arjun Patel: Good callout. p95 increased by about 10% for sequences > 512 tokens. p50 stayed similar. The tail appears when multiple large seq requests align and fill the max_batch; queueing delay + kernel scheduling causes the tail.
[02:06] Ethan Miller: Is this different on dedicated vs hosted?
[02:09] Maya Chen: Slightly. On Dedicated the pool is isolated so the variance is lower, but capacity planning matters — if you set too-high concurrency without enough reserved GPUs you'll see queueing at the ingress. On hosted we can autoscale but cold starts and cross-tenant batching variances can add jitter.
[02:26] Joanna Park: Could we reduce tail by lowering max_batch or by changing the batch window?
[02:30] Arjun Patel: Yes. Two levers: (1) shrink max_batch from 48 to 32 which reduces kernel contention for long sequences; (2) shorten batch window to 8ms which reduces waiting but might lower effective batching efficiency. We ran a couple of quick A/B tests: 32 max_batch + 8ms window gave about 20% uplift over baseline and reduced p95 tail by ~6% compared to 48/12ms.
[02:55] Liam O'Neal: Any impact on throughput variance?
[02:58] Arjun Patel: Slightly higher variance but much better tail behavior for long sequences. Throughput dropped from 1.6k to ~1.45k tokens/sec in that config.
[03:09] Joanna Park: Okay that tradeoff seems reasonable — lower peak but better SLAs. What about queueing policy, do you use FIFO or weighted?
[03:17] Noah Rivera: Right now default is FIFO with some priority for short requests. We can configure a hybrid: give priority to short (<128 token) requests and put long ones into a secondary queue with controlled concurrency. That generally helps user-facing latency.
[03:32] Sara Gomez: How would that affect cost? If long jobs get queued longer, we may need more capacity to keep throughput up.
[03:39] Arjun Patel: Exactly. If you want same throughput with more queueing, you'll need more GPUs or higher concurrency. There's a direct cost delta. We'll quantify that in the spreadsheet.
[03:48] Joanna Park: Any unexpected errors during the run?
[03:51] Arjun Patel: We did see a handful of OOMs on one node when two long sequences aligned and batch packing put them together, so we added a soft limit to prevent packing together sequences > 768 tokens. That eliminated the OOMs in subsequent runs.
[04:08] Liam O'Neal: Did you try quantized model variants? The docs mentioned 8-bit quantization could help throughput.
[04:13] Arjun Patel: We did a quick smoke with a q8 variant — throughput improved ~12% at minor quality delta; but memory behavior changed and cold-start latency increased slightly. For production we'd recommend running evals on your prompt sets.
[04:27] Joanna Park: For the POC we care about p95 under 250ms for user search flows, and background async tasks can tolerate more latency. Can you map which routes should be prioritized?
[04:38] Maya Chen: Sure — typical pattern: prioritize short interactive routes, route long batch jobs to a dedicated pool or to background queue. We'll put a suggested routing table in the runbook.
[04:48] Noah Rivera: Also note that we can fallback to a slightly smaller model variant when under pressure — gives deterministic latencies.
[04:55] Sara Gomez: Is fallback automatic? How do you control quality regression?
[04:58] Arjun Patel: It's policy-driven. We test fallback candidate models with the eval set and set automatic rollback if quality drops beyond threshold. We'll share the eval summary.
[05:06] Joanna Park: Network considerations — our security team wants to run the dedicated test in our VPC. Any special egress or NAT settings?
[05:13] Maya Chen: For dedicated VPC we recommend NAT with outbound rules for model downloads only; runtime traffic stays within region. We'll share a network checklist.
[05:21] Sara Gomez: We'll provision a test VPC by Friday. ETA is end of day Thursday to give you access.
[05:27] Maya Chen: Perfect. Regarding benchmarks — Arjun, you mentioned a 10k-request run?
[05:31] Arjun Patel: Yeah we want to run a 10k-request synthetic with realistic arrival patterns: mix of short (<=64 tokens) 60%, medium (65-256) 30%, long (>256) 10%. We'll include 2x long sequences to stress the tail. We'll capture p50/p90/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:51] Liam O'Neal: For the arrival pattern, can you post the generator so we can reproduce on our side?
[05:55] Arjun Patel: I'll upload the load generator script and the exact config. It's in the runbook folder.
[06:00] Joanna Park: Any changes to RBAC or audit logs we should be aware of during tests?
[06:05] Maya Chen: No changes needed for the POC — audit logs are on by default for Dedicated. We'll share retention and S3 export options.
[06:13] Ethan Miller: Regarding cost — if we move to dedicated to hit steady throughput, what's the break-even?
[06:18] Maya Chen: We'll run the model-level cost delta; rough rule of thumb is dedicated makes sense when you have sustained high utilization and want predictable latency. We'll put a modeled break-even in the spreadsheet based on your expected QPS.
[06:30] Joanna Park: Okay. Any blockers we should call out?
[06:33] Sara Gomez: Need the test VPC, and we need the generator and expected metrics instrumented in our monitoring. That will be done once we have the runbook.
[06:42] Maya Chen: We'll prioritize the runbook and the generator uploads — Arjun will run the 10k test once VPC is ready and share results.
[06:49] Noah Rivera: Small note on logs: sometimes the autogenerated transcripts in the logs have product name variations like "Redwood Ded" in our tools, not a problem but FYI if you search.
[06:58] Joanna Park: Great. Quick recap?
[07:01] Maya Chen: Recap: we saw ~30% throughput uplift at concurrency 16 with 48/12ms batching; p95 tail increased ~10% for >512 tokens. We propose testing a 32/8ms config (reduce max_batch & window) which reduces tail by ~6% but drops throughput to ~1.45k. We'll run 10k synthetic with the arrival mix, test queueing policy (short-first + long-secondary), test on dedicated VPC once provisioned. Redwood to send cost delta and runbook.
[07:36] Joanna Park: Sounds good. Schedule next sync for next Wednesday same time?
[07:40] Maya Chen: Works for us. Thanks everyone.
[07:44] Liam O'Neal: Thanks.
[07:46] Sara Gomez: Bye.
notes: Shared artifacts: runbook link (shared folder), benchmark spreadsheet (sheet:apx-throughput), load generator script (loadgen/v2). Customer will provision VPC and share access.
